title: Content Plan
subtitle: One video a day · one Czech lesson a day

daily.detail: Posted to YouTube Shorts and Instagram Reels — same asset, both places. Not two. One.
15 minutes from the Czech screen. Non-negotiable and non-optional, which is exactly why it's small.

premise: The old plan asked for 2 reels a day, a weekly long form, batching across two shoot days and five content pillars. It was a plan for a production company, not for one person who also runs markets on weekends. You didn't fall behind because you're lazy — you fell behind because it was unbuildable.
So it's two things a day now. One video. One Czech lesson. Everything else in here is support for those two.

The brand is unchanged: you're a **test subject**, not a fitness influencer. You put your own body through things and publish the numbers whether they flatter you or not. That's what lets one channel hold a Viking diet, a Navy SEAL fitness test and a sprint transformation without looking scattered.

spine.name: Marathoner to sprinter
spine.why: You ran Gold Coast in July. Every adaptation in your legs is currently wrong for sprinting — slow-twitch dominant, built for economy instead of force. That conflict is the hook, and nobody else can make that video because it's true about you.
spine.targetNote: Fix the number after the baseline, not before. Sub-13 is fit, sub-12 is genuinely top few percent of adult men, sub-11 is club-athlete. Don't say '1%' on camera until you can defend it.

phases.name: Ramp
phases.focus: Tendon and hamstring prep. Nothing maximal until 1 Oct. This gate is the whole plan's insurance policy.

phases.name: Power
phases.focus: Heavy lower body, plyos, hill sprints. Bodyweight goes up — that's content, not failure.

phases.name: Speed
phases.focus: Max velocity, flying 30s, mechanics. The first real time drops land here.

phases.name: Sharpen & trial
phases.focus: Block starts, race modelling, taper, then the filmed public time trial.

spine.risk: Sprinting off an endurance base is the highest hamstring-tear risk in athletics. Tear one and the arc dies with your leg. Nothing maximal until 1 Oct — this is the one place impatience costs you everything.

formats.name: The Quest
formats.what: The sprint transformation — training, times, setbacks, the numbers on screen.
formats.why: The spine. It's the only reason anyone comes back rather than just watching once.

formats.name: Ancient Protocols
formats.what: 24 hours eating and training as a historical warrior culture.
formats.why: Highest reach per hour of effort you own. Weird, searchable, argument-provoking, cheap to film.

formats.name: The Standard
formats.what: Elite, military and historical fitness tests. Pass or fail, on camera.
formats.why: Built-in stakes and a built-in ending — people watch to find out if you make it.

rhythm.note: One shoot day. Six easy days. The bank never drops below 7 videos — if it does, Monday gets longer, not the other days.

days.what: SHOOT DAY — batch the week's 7 videos in one session. This is the only heavy day.
Post one · Czech lesson · market — grab footage while you're there
Post one · Czech lesson · market · 10 min picking next week's 7 ideas

Ancient Protocols: 24h as a Roman legionary — ~70% grain, posca, cheese. 'Rome conquered the world on porridge.'
24h as a Spartan — black broth. Famously the worst food in the ancient world.
24h as a Viking — skyr, dried cod, ale, no vegetables at all
24h as a Mongol horse archer — mare's milk, dried meat, and yes, the blood
24h as a gladiator — barley and ash. They were deliberately fat. Nobody knows this.
24h as a samurai — rice, miso, fish, no meat
24h as an Aztec eagle warrior — chia, amaranth, spirulina
24h as a Victorian strongman — raw eggs, milk, steak
24h as an ancient Olympian — Milo of Croton reportedly ate 9kg of meat a day
I ate 6,000 calories like an Olympic swimmer
The Standard: The Roman legionary march — 30km in 5 hours carrying 20kg
Navy SEAL PST — can a marathon runner pass?
The NFL combine, as a distance runner
The Cooper test — 12 minutes, elite standard
Ancient Olympic pentathlon — all five events in one day
Firefighter physical ability test in full kit
1896 Olympic gold standards — could you have medalled?
The Quest: Time reveal — 'Day N, here's the clock' (your highest-retention format)
Marathon body vs sprint body — the change, monthly
What I ate today to gain muscle without losing speed
Answering the comment that said I'd never do it
Why I'm not allowed to sprint yet (the hamstring gate explained)

hook: First 1.5 seconds decide it. Number + stake + conflict: 'I ran a marathon in July. Today I'm trying to break 12 seconds.'
Cold open on the strangest visual you have. Never open on your face talking.
On-screen text mirrors the spoken hook — most people watch muted.
No 'hey guys', no 'in this video', no intro.
keep: State the open loop in the first 3 seconds, resolve it at the end.
Cut every 1.5–2.5 seconds. Nothing changing on screen for 3 seconds means they're gone.
Keep a number visible — a timer, the scale, the plate count. It's the reason to stay.
Film the failures. They outperform the wins and they make the wins believable.
share: Argument bait: 'Roman soldiers ate better than you do.'
Number every post — 'Day 41 of 150' says there's a story and they've missed some.
Let comments pick the next diet. Ownership converts watchers into a following.
One thing they could actually do tomorrow.

watch: 3-second retention — want 70%+. Below 60% means the hook failed, not the video.
Shares per view — the best single predictor of something breaking out.
Subscribers per video — the only one that compounds.
rules: Any format that hits 3× your baseline: make 3 more within 7 days.
Any format that underperforms 3 times running: drop it, don't fix it.
Never judge a post before 72 hours — shorts spike late.
Posted daily at 7/10 beats posted weekly at 9/10. Consistency is the whole game at this stage.

money.note: Optimise for reach now; build so the money works later without a jarring pivot.
points: YouTube Partner Program, shorts route: 1,000 subs + 10 million shorts views in 90 days. One video a day makes this slower than the old plan but actually achievable.
Dropping the weekly long form costs you the watch-hours route to monetisation. That's a real trade — take it for now, and add long form back only when a single video obviously deserves it.
Pre-workout affiliate isn't live: no brand mentions, and don't sign a competing supplement deal in the meantime.
Show pre-workout unbranded in training footage now, so it reads as continuity later rather than a sellout moment.

notes: The Czech lesson is a daily fixture, not content — but if a day's lesson gives you something genuinely funny or hard, 30 seconds of it is a free second series. Optional. Don't let it become a second job.
Real Life (markets, NRICH, Brisbane) lives in stories now, not in the daily video. It's the trust layer and it shouldn't eat a production slot.
